title: Construct-validity testing reveals that scIB bio-conservation metrics predict cross-tissue transfer but invert cross-assay rankings at chance
description: A three-check construct-validity protocol (null-model discrimination, cross-dimensionality robustness, sign-correctness) applied to five preregistered geometric modules and the field-standard scIB bio-conservation suite for evaluating single-cell foundation model embeddings. The scIB audit finds 46-58% pairwise inversion rates against cross-assay transfer F1 (at or worse than chance), while a preregistered cross-tissue replication finds positive prediction (rho = +0.63, p = 0.0014), localizing the failure to the cross-assay setting. Two confirmatory tests show metric rankings are stable across hyperparameters but metric values are non-monotonic under controlled noise. This archive contains the manuscript (v15), source code, experiment scripts, raw results from experiments 0-11, preregistration documents with SHA-256 frozen scorer code, and seed-stability replication data.
